title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page is a section title only, written in the top right corner: 'Les foncteurs de Hodge sur la catégorie des motifs. (Comparaison des deux foncteurs, alg[ébriques] et transcendants)'. In modern terms it announces a study of the Hodge realization functors on the Q-linear Tannakian category of (pure) motives M over a field k of characteristic 0 embedded in C. There are two realizations. The algebraic one is de Rham cohomology H_dR, a fibre functor over k carrying the Hodge filtration. The transcendental one is Betti cohomology H_B, a fibre functor over Q carrying a Q-structure. The comparison isomorphism H_B ⊗ C ≅ H_dR ⊗_k C relates them. Equivalently, there is a torsor of isomorphisms Isom^⊗(ω_dR, ω_B ⊗ k) under the motivic Galois group G, and the period matrix is a C-point of this torsor. The page sits between two related pages. The previous page asks whether, for an elliptic curve over Q̄, the period point g in G(C)/G(Q̄) has transcendence degree equal to dim G; this is Grothendieck's period conjecture in a special case. It also asks about transcendence of the Hodge splitting. The next page compares analytic (algebraic, residue-defined) and topological fundamental classes, finding a universal factor λ^p (λ = 1/2πi). That is exactly the compatibility of cycle classes with the Betti/de Rham comparison, needed so the Hodge functor is well defined on motives with rational structure. So the planned chapter covers: the Hodge realization of motives (Q-Hodge structure = Betti lattice plus de Rham Hodge filtration via comparison); compatibility of cycle classes up to (2πi)^p; and the period torsor and its transcendence properties.

ideas.what: Hodge realization functor on the category of motives, built from the algebraic (de Rham) and transcendental (Betti) fibre functors and their comparison
ideas.modern_name: Hodge/Betti/de Rham realizations of motives; comparison isomorphism; period torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motives, 1960s), formalized by Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne (1979 Hodge cycles, 1989), Deligne–Milne (1982); period torsor viewpoint by André, Kontsevich–Zagier
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via letters/Saavedra's thesis and the IHES motives seminar; the period conjecture appears in Grothendieck's 1966 de Rham paper footnote (in a special case) and was later stated by André

deep.surprise_reason: The page is only a section heading announcing the comparison of the de Rham and Betti fibre functors (Hodge realization). This is standard, well-documented motivic material with no new mathematics on the page.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 reads 'deux fonct. alg.' (fonct[eurs] alg[ébriques]), not 'deux fonct. fib.[?]'; the full parenthesis is '(Comparaison des deux fonct. alg. et transcendants)'.
